title: Apply and verify
intro: The tool runs the command in a fresh terminal session (as if you had just opened a new terminal), optionally sends one minimal test request to the service gateway, and tells you plainly whether it worked. On failure it explains the cause and how to fix it.

reminder.title: Before you start: close every terminal window
reminder.body: That includes Windows Terminal, PowerShell, CMD, Git Bash, macOS Terminal / iTerm, and the built-in terminals of VS Code, Cursor and similar editors. Terminals that are already open cannot see the new configuration.

card.title: Verify {{tool}}
card.description: Runs {{command}} in a fresh session to confirm the command can be found and executed.

gateway.toggle: Also test the gateway connection (requires your API key, once)
gateway.description: Sends one minimal test request to the gateway to confirm the address, protocol and key are correct.
gateway.keyNote: The key is held in memory only for this one request: it is cleared as soon as the request is sent and is never stored, logged, uploaded or written to a report.
gateway.notHttps: This address is not https, so the key would travel unencrypted. The tool only sends the key over https; use the service gateway address.
gateway.missingFields: Enter the gateway address, model and API key before verifying.

actions.finishAnyway: Finish anyway, even with failures (you can come back later)

results.overallFail: {{tool}} is not working yet — see the diagnosis below.

errorClass.not_https: Address is not https — the key was not sent

terminals.title: {{count}} terminal window(s) still running
terminals.body: These windows will not see the new configuration, and verification may fail because of them. Close them all (for editor terminals, quit the whole editor), then re-check.

diagnosis.title: Diagnosis
diagnosis.autoOpened: Verification failed; the tool has analysed the cause automatically.
diagnosis.merged: Results from the full environment snapshot have been merged in.
